% Pictures that need a conversion or that lie outside the document's folder.
% Each must be a file inside the page's folder, named by a src that does not
% leave it, and nothing is written outside the build and page folders.
% PDF pictures: without and with the extension, starred, a page of a
% two-page PDF, in a subfolder by name and by \graphicspath, with a space in
% the name (whose bounding box TeX cannot read) at its natural size, with a
% height, a scale, or a width and height kept in proportion, with options, with no size, with a height or a scale alone, in
% a figure with a caption, in a minipage, in a
% footnote, and in a link. EPS pictures, converted by Ghostscript. Pictures
% named with ../ (by \graphicspath, by name, two levels up, the same name in
% two parent folders, a name with a space, PNG, JPEG, PDF, and EPS), the same
% picture twice, an import.sty chapter, an \import from a parent folder, and
% epsfig. A PDF beside the document, one found by kpathsea, one with the name
% of another in another folder, one with dots in its name, in display math,
% and in a subfigure; an EPS picture without its extension. A PDF and an EPS
% picture in parentheses, and two PDF pictures half the line wide side by
% side, with no space before them. A PDF and an EPS picture with the same
% name in one folder, and a PDF beside a PNG named as its conversion was
% (own.pdf and own-1.png). A picture inside the folder is a guard.
% run.mjs builds this page again with \PdfpicAbsolute and \PdfpicAbsolutePdf
% set to absolute paths of a PNG and a PDF picture.
